app.title: gathervis: pre-stack seismic gather viewer
app.summary: A person opens a set of recorded seismic shots in the browser, optionally with source and receiver coordinates. They check the acquisition layout over a map of how many traces fall in each midpoint bin, and tap a source to open its shot record. They step through shots with a slider or the arrow keys, re-sort each shot's traces, and change the display, filter and gain until events stand out. Then they draw windows to take amplitude and f-k spectra, pick first breaks by hand or with an STA/LTA trigger, and draw top and bottom mutes. They come away with exported picks, mute lines, analysis windows and full-resolution images.

task.text: Quality-check recorded seismic shot gathers one shot at a time, measure their frequency content, and pick first breaks and mute lines that carry across the whole survey.

data.text: A survey of seismic recordings: for each shot, many receiver traces sampled over time, with optional source and receiver coordinates. Large files are read lazily from memory-mapped arrays or SEG-Y.
data.item: a shot gather: every receiver trace recorded for one source, laid out as trace against time

stage.text: quality-checking raw pre-stack shot records during processing, before velocity analysis and stacking

mechanism.text: A geometry map with the fold underneath and a shot-gather panel share one cursor, so tapping a source and moving the shot slider or arrow keys both select the same shot. Display and processing settings in a sidebar redraw the panel, and tools on the panel (analysis windows, picks, mute nodes) are stored by trace or offset so they follow the data through shot changes and re-sorts.

field.text: pre-stack seismic data processing and QC in exploration geophysics

workflow.name: step through recordings, condition them, and mark events to export

steps.here: A NumPy array, raw binary memmap or SEG-Y file is loaded, with source and receiver coordinates taken from an .npz file or from the trace headers.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The Geometry tab draws sources and receivers over a CMP fold map. Bin size can be edited, and the grid, live bins, fold range and trace total are listed as a geometry check. Tapping a source opens that shot.

steps.step: step through items one at a time
steps.here: A shot slider, a shot-number box, ←/→ (Shift steps ten, Home/End jump to the ends) and a Sort selector that lays traces out as recorded, by receiver line, by offset or by azimuth.

steps.step: condition the display so the signal shows
steps.here: Density or wiggle display, colormap, clip percentile, polarity flip, an Ormsby low-, high- or band-pass filter, and AGC or trace-balance gain. All of it is applied per shot as it is drawn.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Box or polygon windows drawn on the gather give amplitude spectra (per trace, mean or middle trace, in linear or dB) and an f-k spectrum of the first window.

Click to place first-break or event picks, run gapped STA/LTA auto-picking and snap picks to a peak or trough. Top and bottom mutes are drawn as nodes stored against offset, with a survey-wide default and per-gather exceptions.
Picks go out as CSV (shot, trace, time_s), mutes and windows as JSON, and the gather as a full-resolution PNG. The view's state sits in the URL so it can be shared.

distinctive: Fold is computed from coordinates alone, so the survey overview costs nothing however large the trace data is
Picks are stored against the trace and mutes against offset, not the screen column, so they survive re-sorting and carry over to other shots
Mute lines have one survey-wide default plus per-gather exceptions, with Make default and Revert, and a taper so the cut does not add false energy
The same 3-D shot can be re-laid out by acquisition order, receiver line, offset or azimuth on one 2-D panel
Spectra use the raw gated samples with no taper or smoothing, and report the frequency spacing of the window
